iut_type: OS-version-only re-listing (Sony TV) -- RF/RF PHY ICS discrepancy between old and new referenced QDID combination, resolved by switching to a matching SoC Subset variant
customer_question: This registration is a re-listing of a 3-year-old registration, triggered purely by an OS version upgrade -- no wireless module or RF spec change. We believe the RF/RF PHY test report from the original registration can be reused -- is that correct?
question_variants: If nothing about the wireless hardware changed, can the entire prior registration just be carried forward without any new analysis?
If the new Controller Subsystem QDID doesn't exactly match the old one's RF/RF PHY parameters, what are the options?
actual_issue: The customer assumed that since no wireless module or RF specification had changed, the prior registration's RF/RF PHY test report could simply be reused as-is for the new OS-version-driven re-listing. However, a layer-by-layer comparison between the original registration and the new registration's referenced Controller Subsystem QDID revealed a genuine RF/RF PHY ICS discrepancy (a Power Class-related item differed between 'NO' and 'YES'), meaning the new QDID combination wasn't a perfect match even though the underlying intent was an unchanged re-listing.
plain_english_explanation: Yes, the RF/RF PHY test report can be reused as long as the wireless module and RF specification are genuinely unchanged -- but this must be verified explicitly rather than assumed, by comparing the new registration's referenced QDID against the original registration's actual RF/RF PHY ICS line items. In this case, the comparison revealed a real mismatch: LL item 9/15 (Power Class 1) and RF item 1/1 (Power Class 1) were declared 'NO' in the original registration but 'YES' in the newly-referenced QDID. Fixing this by directly editing the LL layer's ICS to match would be technically possible, but under the post-July-2024 registration system, any LL ICS edit triggers a full LL Test Plan with roughly 300 test items requiring lab testing and report upload -- making this approach impractical in terms of both cost and timeline. Compounding the problem, the new QDID combination itself also had its own inter-layer inconsistency, and resolving that via ICS edits in a trial Project surfaced yet further new-layer test requirements. The practical solution was to use a different Subset variant of the same SoC: the chipset offers four Subset variants, and one of them shares the same RF/RF PHY Class (Class 2) as the original registration's referenced component, and combining that specific Subset with the rest of the registration does not produce any inter-layer inconsistency. Switching the referenced QDID to that matching Subset avoided both the expensive LL retest and the inter-layer inconsistency problem simultaneously.
consultant_answer: Yes, if the wireless module and RF spec are genuinely unchanged, the RF/RF PHY test report can be reused -- but we checked this explicitly rather than assuming it, and found a real discrepancy: the new QDID combination's Power Class declaration (LL 9/15, RF 1/1) doesn't match your original registration. Editing the LL ICS to fix this directly would trigger a ~300-item LL Test Plan under the current system, which isn't practical. Instead, we recommend switching to a specific Subset variant of the same SoC (one of four available) that shares the same RF/RF PHY Class as your original registration and doesn't produce an inter-layer inconsistency when combined -- this avoids both the expensive retest and the consistency problem.
decision_logic: When a customer assumes an OS-version-only re-listing means the prior RF/RF PHY test report and referenced QDID combination carry forward unchanged, explicitly verify the new registration's referenced QDID against the original registration's RF/RF PHY ICS line items rather than taking the 'nothing changed' assumption at face value -- a discrepancy may exist even without any actual hardware change, and if found, check whether an alternative SoC Subset variant matches the original RF/RF PHY Class before resorting to a costly direct LL ICS edit.
final_recommendation: For any registration framed as a 'simple' re-listing or carryover, run an explicit RF/RF PHY ICS comparison between the old and new referenced components before assuming the prior test report and reference structure can be reused unchanged, and check for alternative component Subset variants that might avoid both retest cost and inter-layer inconsistency if a mismatch is found.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming an OS-version-only re-listing requires no RF/RF PHY verification could result in a registration with an undetected ICS mismatch, or alternatively, discovering the mismatch late could force a costly ~300-item LL retest under time pressure if the Subset-switching alternative isn't considered.
